description: Savor the authentic taste of India with this mouth-watering Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken. Marinated in a rich blend of yogurt and aromatic spices, each bite offers a smoky, tender, and incredibly flavorful experience. Perfect for a hearty dinner, this recipe brings the magic of the tandoor to your backyard grill.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken
instructions.text: Wash and pat dry the chicken pieces thoroughly. Make deep gashes on each piece, especially on the breast and thigh, to allow the marinade to penetrate well. In a large bowl, combine the Greek yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, tandoori masala, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, salt, mustard oil, and optional food color. Mix everything until well combined to form a thick marinade.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: Add the chicken pieces to the marinade, ensuring each piece is fully coated. Rub the marinade into the gashes. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, for best results. The longer the marination, the more flavorful and tender the chicken will be.

instructions.title: Prepare the Charcoal Grill
instructions.text: About 30 minutes before grilling, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the charcoal to create a two-zone cooking area: one side for direct high heat and the other for indirect lower heat. Let the coals burn until they are covered with a fine gray ash, indicating they are ready for cooking. Clean and oil the grill grates.

instructions.title: Grill the Chicken
instructions.text: Place the marinated chicken pieces directly over the hot coals (direct heat zone) for about 3-4 minutes per side, turning frequently, until they develop a nice char and smoky flavor. Be careful not to burn them. This initial searing helps lock in juices and creates the characteristic Tandoori crust.

instructions.title: Continue Cooking Indirectly
instructions.text: Move the chicken pieces to the indirect heat zone of the grill. Close the lid and continue cooking for another 15-20 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C). Turn the chicken occasionally and baste with melted butter or oil during the last 10 minutes of cooking to keep it moist and add richness.

instructions.title: Final Touches and Serving
instructions.text: Once cooked, remove the Tandoori chicken from the grill. You can lightly char it again over direct heat for a minute or two if desired for extra smoky flavor. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice. Serve hot with mint chutney, sliced onions, and naan bread or rice.

tips: For truly authentic flavor, ensure your yogurt is thick and drained of excess water. This prevents the marinade from becoming too watery and helps it cling better to the chicken.
Do not overcrowd the grill. Cook the chicken in batches if necessary to maintain consistent grill temperature and ensure even cooking and browning.
A crucial step for tender chicken is the long marination time. Aim for at least 8 hours or overnight to allow the acids in the yogurt and spices to tenderize the meat effectively.
article:
Mastering the art of authentic Indian cuisine at home often feels like a daunting task, but some dishes are simply too irresistible not to try. Among them, Tandoori Chicken stands as a crowned jewel, beloved for its vibrant color, tantalizing aroma, and succulent, smoky flavor. While traditionally cooked in a high-heat clay oven called a tandoor, achieving that signature char and tenderness is remarkably possible right in your backyard with a charcoal grill. This guide will walk you through creating a spectacular Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken that will transport your taste buds straight to the streets of Delhi or the finest Indian restaurants, making it an ideal Indian dinner recipe for any occasion.

## What is Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled?

Tandoori Chicken is a classic North Indian dish featuring chicken marinated in yogurt and a rich blend of spices, then traditionally cooked in a tandoor oven. The yogurt acts as a tenderizer, while the spices – including ginger, garlic, garam masala, turmeric, cumin, and red chili powder – infuse the chicken with an explosion of flavor. The characteristic reddish hue often comes from a touch of food coloring, but can also be achieved naturally with Kashmiri chili powder or paprika, which offer color without excessive heat.

When prepared as Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken, the process aims to replicate the intense, dry heat and smoky essence of a tandoor. The charcoal grill provides direct, high heat that quickly chars the exterior, locking in juices and developing that coveted smoky flavor profile. The result is chicken that is wonderfully tender on the inside with a beautifully crisp, subtly smoky crust on the outside, a true testament to the magic of open-flame cooking. It's a dish that promises both culinary adventure and comforting familiarity, making it a star Indian dinner recipe.

## Ingredients You Need

To create your own unforgettable Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken, gather these fresh and flavorful ingredients:

For the Chicken:
*   8-10 boneless, skinless chicken thighs (or 4 bone-in, skin-on chicken leg quarters, halved) – about 2-2.5 lbs total
*   2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice

For the Marinade:
*   1 cup full-fat plain Greek yogurt (or hung curd for thicker consistency)
*   2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste (equal parts fresh ginger and garlic, crushed)
*   1 tablespoon Kashmiri red chili powder (for color and mild heat)
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon black pepper
*   1/2 teaspoon dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), crushed (optional, but highly recommended for authentic flavor)
*   1/2 teaspoon red food coloring (optional, for vibrant color)
*   1 tablespoon mustard oil (or any neutral oil)
*   1 teaspoon salt, or to taste

For Grilling:
*   Charcoal briquettes or lump charcoal
*   Wood chips (hickory, apple, or mesquite for added smoke, optional)
*   Oil for brushing the grill grates

For Garnish (Optional):
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped
*   Lemon wedges
*   Sliced red onions

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps to prepare your succulent Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken:

1.  **Prepare the Chicken**: If using bone-in chicken, make 2-3 deep slits on each piece to allow the marinade to penetrate deeply. If using boneless thighs, simply pat them dry. Place the chicken in a large bowl and sprinkle with fresh lemon juice. Rub it in and let sit for 10 minutes. This helps tenderize the chicken and allows the marinade to adhere better.
2.  **Make the Marinade**: In a separate large bowl, combine the Greek yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri red chili powder, ground cumin, ground coriander, turmeric powder, garam masala, black pepper, crushed dried fenugreek leaves, red food coloring (if using), mustard oil, and salt. Mix thoroughly until all spices are well incorporated and you have a smooth, thick paste.
3.  **Marinate the Chicken**: Add the lemon-coated chicken to the marinade bowl. Using your hands (gloves recommended!), massage the marinade into every piece of chicken, ensuring it gets into the slits. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight (up to 24 hours) for maximum flavor and tenderness.
4.  **Prepare the Grill**: About 30-40 minutes before you plan to cook, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange charcoal for a two-zone fire: a direct high-heat zone and an indirect medium-heat zone. For lump charcoal, aim for a temperature of 375-400°F (190-205°C). If using wood chips for extra smoke, add them to the hot coals about 10 minutes before placing the chicken on the grill. Ensure your grill grates are clean and oiled to prevent sticking.
5.  **Grill the Chicken**: Remove the chicken from the refrigerator and let it sit at room temperature for about 15-20 minutes while the grill heats up. Place the marinated chicken directly over the high-heat zone. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side to get a nice char, being careful not to burn it.
6.  **Finish Cooking Indirectly**: Once charred, move the chicken to the indirect heat zone. Close the grill lid and cook for another 15-25 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C). Flip the chicken every 5-7 minutes to ensure even cooking. The cooking time will vary depending on the thickness of your chicken pieces and your grill's temperature.
7.  **Rest and Serve**: Once cooked, remove the Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken from the grill and let it rest on a cutting board for 5-10 minutes before serving. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring tender and moist chicken.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

*   **Deep Cuts are Key**: For bone-in chicken, making deep gashes allows the marinade to penetrate to the bone, infusing flavor throughout and ensuring even cooking.
*   **Marinate Longer**: The longer the marination, the better the flavor and tenderness. Overnight is ideal for this Indian dinner recipe.
*   **Use Full-Fat Greek Yogurt**: Its thick consistency clings better to the chicken, and the fat helps keep the chicken moist. If using regular yogurt, strain it through a cheesecloth for an hour or two to remove excess whey.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Grill**: Cook in batches if necessary. Overcrowding lowers the grill temperature and steams the chicken instead of searing it, preventing that beautiful char.
*   **Monitor Heat**: Keep an eye on your charcoal. If the chicken is charring too quickly, move it to a cooler spot on the grill. If it's cooking too slowly, add more hot coals.
*   **Baste (Optional)**: Some chefs like to baste the chicken with a little melted butter or oil during the last few minutes of cooking for extra richness and shine.
*   **Rest the Chicken**: This crucial step ensures juicy, tender results. Don't skip it!
*   **Embrace the Char**: A little char is desirable for authentic Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken flavor; it's what gives it that signature tandoor taste.

## Serving Suggestions

Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is a showstopper on its own, but it truly shines when served as part of a complete Indian feast. Here are some classic accompaniments:

*   **Naan or Roti**: Warm, fluffy naan bread or whole wheat roti are perfect for scooping up the chicken and any leftover juices.
*   **Mint Chutney or Raita**: A refreshing mint-coriander chutney or a cooling cucumber raita provides a lovely contrast to the spicy chicken.
*   **Salad**: A simple kachumber salad (diced cucumbers, tomatoes, and onions with a lemon dressing) adds freshness and crunch.
*   **Lemon Wedges and Sliced Onions**: A squeeze of fresh lemon juice brightens the flavors, and raw onion slices offer a piquant bite.
*   **Basmati Rice**: Fluffy basmati rice or a simple jeera rice (cumin rice) can round out the meal beautifully.
*   **Dal or Vegetable Curry**: For a more elaborate Indian dinner recipe, serve alongside a lentil dish (dal) or a mild vegetable curry.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is hard to beat, there are ways to adapt this recipe to suit different tastes and dietary needs:

*   **Different Cuts of Chicken**: You can use chicken breasts, drumsticks, or even a whole spatchcocked chicken. Adjust grilling times accordingly; breasts will cook faster, while a whole chicken will take longer.
*   **Vegetarian Tandoori**: Marinate paneer cubes, thick slices of bell peppers, onions, zucchini, or mushrooms in the same tandoori marinade. Skewer them and grill until tender and slightly charred.
*   **Spice Level**: Adjust the amount of red chili powder to your preference. For more heat, add a pinch of cayenne pepper. For less, reduce the Kashmiri chili powder.
*   **No Grill? No Problem (Almost!)**: While the smoky flavor of Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is unique, you can achieve delicious results in an oven or air fryer.
    *   **Oven Method**: Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). Place marinated chicken on a baking rack over a foil-lined baking sheet. Bake for 25-35 minutes, flipping halfway, until cooked through. For char, broil for the last 5 minutes, watching carefully.
    *   **Air Fryer Method**: Preheat air fryer to 375°F (190°C). Place chicken in a single layer (do not overcrowd) and cook for 18-25 minutes, flipping halfway, until cooked through and nicely browned.
*   **Smoky Flavor Enhancement**: If using an oven or air fryer, you can impart a smoky flavor by placing a small piece of burning charcoal in a heatproof bowl within the cooking appliance (carefully and briefly) and covering it for a few minutes. This is called *dhungar* and is a traditional Indian technique.

Bringing the vibrant flavors of India into your home kitchen has never been easier or more rewarding. This Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken recipe is a fantastic way to enjoy an authentic Indian dinner, offering a balance of smoky char, tender meat, and aromatic spices that will impress everyone at your table. So fire up your grill, embrace the intoxicating aromas, and get ready to savor every delicious bite!
